Michelle Lynn Gill, PhD Applied Research Manager, NVIDIA BioNeMo Team michelle@michellelynngill.com GitHub | LinkedIn | Personal Website Overview I am an Applied Research Manager on NVIDIA’s BioNeMo team, where I lead a cross-functional effort to train NVIDIA’s Nemotron reasoning models for chemistry and drug-discovery applications. My team develops post-training and evaluation data, benchmarks, and metrics that guide model development. Previously, as a Senior Data Scientist and Machine Learning Engineer at BenevolentAI, I applied machine learning to study drug mechanisms and predict ligand binding poses and affinities. Earlier, as a postdoctoral fellow in Arthur Palmer’s group at Columbia University, I developed and applied nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spin relaxation experiments to study how enzyme dynamics shape biological function. Education 2003-2006 Ph.D., Molecular Biophysics & Biochemistry Yale University, New Haven, CT Thesis: Development of 205Tl NMR methods for the direct study of monovalent metal ions and ligands in nucleic acids Advisors: J. Patrick Loria and Scott Strobel 2001-2003 M.Phil., Molecular Biophysics & Biochemistry Yale University, New Haven, CT 1997-2001 B.S., Biochemistry University of Kansas, Lawrence, KS Highest
